        "feedback": "Mechanism not supported by the code, and not reproduced. (1) bash-jobs.ts spawnShell hands the command to `bash -o pipefail -c` verbatim; the only change is a prepended command_not_found_handle definition (instrumentMissingCommandFailures). No $ rewrite there or in bash.ts. (2) Background jobs run as a transient systemd SERVICE, which expands $ in ExecStart args, so systemd-scope.ts buildTaskArgv runs escapeSystemdServiceArgument (every $ -> $$) for kind===service only. grep -c escapeSystemdServiceArgument = 2 at BOTH the reported runtime sha 7708e704d9 and HEAD, with a --pipe positive control = 1 at both (it landed in a7825d130a, 2026-08-24, before the 2026-09-27 observation). systemd-scope.test.ts (~L76-122) pins the round trip for $VAR, $$ and ${PIPESTATUS[0]}. (3) Live probe, run_in_background:true at the build serving this session (sha not recorded; not tied to 7708e704d9): `L=abc.log; echo \"[$L] [$L.old] ${PIPESTATUS[0]}\"; echo \"$$L\"` printed [abc.log] [abc.log.old] 0 and 1112915L. So \"$L\" is NOT mangled, and the report's <digits>L shape is exactly what bash prints for a literal $$L: the shell saw $$L. What is unestablished is who put the second $ there: caller-side text/JSON/heredoc escaping in the reporter's own command, or a double-escape on some path I did not enumerate (callers of buildTaskArgv/wrapScope not audited). The filer marks it unconfirmed and not reproduced; major severity is not earned.           "title": "A cancelled blueprint operation whose work-item no worker has applied can never settle: cancel only marks it, and every other writer is refused",
          "summary": "Observed 2026-10-06 14:30-14:45Z (su-7f8d7809, plan crm-agent-sales-onboarding-apps-2026-10-06 P-010). The live E2E submitted crm onboarding-step (receipt 38) creating WI-10006707 (harness crm, kind crm-proposal, unassigned), then cancelled it through the seam: cancelBlueprintOperation (packages/operator-core/lib/blueprint/operation-service.ts ~L680) returned accepted:true, handled:false, effected:false and only stamped payload.blueprintCancellation. 15 minutes later the item is still open. Placement skips it (coord-program-workflow excludes blueprintCancellation; operation-worker-binding requireUncancelled), so no worker will ever take it, and a direct work_items:set_state dropped through the app invoker is refused: \"blueprint operation effect refused: accepted operation item requires its applied worker\". Result: every cancel before a worker applies leaves a permanent open, unplaceable item and an operation stuck in cancelling. Proposed fix: when cancel finds no applied worker binding on an unsettled item, settle it to a cancelled/dropped terminal state inside the same transaction (the operator is the authority when no executor exists); add a test that cancel-before-apply reaches phase terminal / outcome cancelled. Live example left in place: WI-10006707. Evidence: papercusp/.papercusp/scratch/p010/e2e-2.log, drop-3.log."

          "kind": "bug",
          "title": "fleet:assignments omits per-member scheduler claim state and cap fields",
          "summary": "Suspected, unconfirmed runtime contract gap. On 2026-10-25, `scheduler:get_claim_spec({ cupId: \"su-6c30dac5-f3fb-4c45-937e-34ee5ed96cc2\" })` resolved fleet revision 16 with `maxConcurrentClaims: 2`. A filtered `fleet:assignments` read for that owner returned `summary.claims: 40` and `work_item_load: 40` (40 claim rows marked active), but omitted `summary.scheduler_claim_state_status`, `summary.scheduler_active_work_item_claims`, and the agent's `schedulerClaimState`.         "feedback": "This report documents a transport refusal from the native-owner direct-wrapper route, not a scheduler implementation failure. `native_tool_owner_unsupported_capability` means the owner RPC refuses to forward the host-local authenticatedPrincipal; under the stated client contract, treat it as a transport refusal and switch the remaining calls to the authenticated ptool CLI.           "title": "consult:close by the requester leaves the dispatched answering session running with no stop signal",
          "summary": "Observed 2026-10-27 on consult conv-mvq2x83t-0000-2212927f6ee640f8aa2857b0a5181c49 (requester su-4aab087c, origin EI-25940249793936216, cascade flavor decision-review).\n\nTimeline (harness_shared.consult_state + the answering session's own transcript):\n- 02:41:13Z consult created by consult:get_feedback (set_blocker decision-review cascade).\n- 02:43:37Z dispatch: full Claude/fable session launched as su-4d187f6c-066b-4679-9e6a-78c0535cb5fa ('convert' of su-ac5c6b74's transcript), host registered after 126ms.\n- 02:50:49Z requester closed the consult `cant_help` with reason \"created accidentally by classifying the fleet leader's D-334 route dependency as a product-owner decision\".\n- ~02:56Z the answering session, having read the thread, plan_decisions, two work-items and the source transcript (~13 minutes of work), called consult:reply and was refused `consult_not_open` (state closed_cant_help). No signal of the closure reached it in between: no coord inject, no wake, no [coord+N] line.\n\nDefect: closing (or declining/expiring) a consult does not cancel or notify the in-flight dispatched answerer. The answering session only learns on its terminal write, after the full research cost has been paid. consult_state.dispatch_attempts records answeringOwnerId, so the recipient is known.\n\nProposed fix: in consult:close (and the decline/expiry paths) when dispatch_attempts has a dispatched answeringOwnerId whose session is live, (a) mark the dispatch cancelled in consult_state and (b) coord:send that owner a stand-down with wake:'required' (summary 'consult <id> closed <state> — stop; do not reply') so the next tool round surfaces it as a [coord+N] line. Optionally the answering session's launch brief should carry an `events:await consult:closed:<conversation_id>` key so the harness can inject the closure mid-turn. Recurrence guard: a test that closes a consult with a live dispatched answerer and asserts the stand-down message exists in coord for that ownerId.\n\nSeparate, smaller signal (not a second record): the requester's reason says the consult was auto-created from a set_blocker product-decision cascade for what was a fleet-leader routing question — the cascade had no 'this is a fleet-leader question, route to @fleet-leader:<slug>' branch, so a full external answerer was spent on it."
        },

The routineProbeFailed response now retains reason, elapsedMs and available errorMessage so future failures are diagnosable instead of only a generic warning. Conventional regression controls cover active scope with/without an explicit wrong-scope argument, actual facts-reader errors, and timeouts.         "feedback": "This filing does not establish a product defect. The measured 429 is `mcp_proxy_overloaded` with `forwardingResult: not_forwarded`, which means the proxy intentionally rejected the request before the operator executed it. The current proxy code bounds ordinary FIFO admission, and its tests assert that overflow returns a retryable 429 with not_forwarded. The report also says the query was not retried and prescribes ptool as the authorized fallback. Re-run the transcript receipt lookup through ptool; do not infer the receipt is absent.           "kind": "bug",
          "title": "scorecards:get per-criterion reads too slow to page a 9-criterion card inside one code:run (55s nested timeout)",
          "summary": "Observed 2026-10-13 ~21:16Z during grading-integrity audit of EI-25900285445623116 (build 78cd58273a, :3070). A code:run looping scorecards:get {issueId, criterionKey, evidenceOffset:0} over 6 criterion keys (each evidence <=1086 chars, complete in one page) failed with `request_timeout: nested tool \"code:run\" exceeded 55000ms via tools:invoke`. That implies more than 9s per small per-criterion read. The grading-integrity brief and card both require reading every criterion's evidence through this paged per-criterion door. Auditors therefore cannot batch it in code:run as the playbook recommends. They fall back to N parallel direct calls, and those then trip the aggregate output budget: 7 of 12 parallel calls spilled to scratch with 'aggregate-output-budget-exceeded', so each needed extra capability:read turns. Cause UNKNOWN / unconfirmed: possibly each criterionKey read recomputes the full card (currentness, evidenceBindingCurrentness, auditTarget) per call. The box also reported 'Perf budget breached (ambient)' at the time, so load correlation is possible; that is still a bug per the responsiveness design. Suggested fix: one call returning all criteria's complete evidence when it fits a size bound (e.g. criterionKeys:[...] or evidence:'all'), and/or cache the per-card currentness computation across criterion pages. Repro: code:run { script: for 6 keys await tools.scorecards.get({issueId:'EI-25900285445623116', criterionKey:k, evidenceOffset:0}) }."
        },

          "title": "judge carry-respawn drops the kickoff brief and the judge role cannot read its own transcript to recover it",
          "summary": "Observed 2026-10-21 08:51-09:03Z, session su-2ea0f358-8c3f-41ce-bfed-bb6379290c4c (role judge), grading-integrity audit of scorecard EI-26577353033210593 (audit card EI-26579054352729640).\n\nWhat happened: the papercusp MCP transport dropped mid-audit. The mcp-dark-watchdog (P-005) resumed the session from a deterministic carry document built 2026-10-21T08:51:08Z. That carry document has no copy of the kickoff brief (the first user turn naming the subject, the lease key/reservedAt, the emit tool and the expected output). It holds only the session's own last verbatim turns. The lease key and reservedAt survived only because the pre-drop turn happened to quote them in prose.\n\nThe judge role persona says: \"If the brief is missing ... do NOT infer a mission and do NOT grade.\" The documented recovery is sessions:search / sessions:read { session:'self' }, but for this principal it is refused:\n- tools:invoke sessions:search -> role_not_allowed: Role \"judge\" cannot call tool \"sessions:search\" (allowed: scoper, architect, worker, validator, reviewer, debugger, operator, mug, documenter, curator, papercup, kettle, release-fixer)\n- memory:get -> missing_capability memory:read\n- search:fulltext -> missing_capability search:read\n- capability:bash -> missing_capability capability:bash\n\nSo a resumed judge must either stop, or reconstruct the brief from the target card plus the scorecards:emit schema. I did the latter: gradingAuditReservation key/reservedAt read off the card's gradingAudit.dispatchReservation. It worked here only because the emit schema documents the lease field.\n\nExpected (either fix closes it): (a) the carry document for a mission-launched role (judge / any kickoff-brief role) re-injects the kickoff brief verbatim; or (b) the judge role may read its OWN transcript (sessions:read/search with session:'self' only, no cross-session reads), which keeps least privilege.\n\nCause not proven: I could not read the carry-document builder (no bash/grep), so whether the builder deliberately omits the first turn or simply ages it out of the tail is unknown."
        },
